mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent decline in the RSAFS (personal savings) signals liquidity injection into a savings-heavy environment, boosting risk appetite and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% and RSAFS declines month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for four consecutive months signals high inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL exceeds 4% for four consecutive months.
